title: RAW_UNREVIEWED: multilingual inflectional feature bundles constrain singleton completions without lexical cell copying
summary: A source-owned trilingual paradigm supplies person/number and tense oppositions while its Latin, Persian and Cuman cells remain different words. Under a frozen target production inventory, existential unknown-word completions would receive only shared feature bundles, preserving all old values and adding no production or singleton gloss.

design.source_example: Kuun1880 Codex Cumanicus p.1 contains complete six-person present and imperfect tables aligned across Latin, Persian and Cuman. The source supplies row/tense content relations; it does not license copying any source cell into a target word.
design.mechanism: Keep the frozen target productions and all 47 retained values unchanged. For each unknown whole form in a predeclared complete reading, assign an existential feature bundle only: person/number, tense or aspect contrast, and paradigm-slot participation. Repeated forms retain one bundle; distinct forms may realize distinct bundles. A complete candidate must cover a declared finite opposition set, such as six person/number slots in one present frame and the corresponding imperfect frame, without requiring identical lexical strings across language-like channels.
design.joint_content_consequence: A repeated unknown whole that occupies the same participant slot across two complete readings must preserve its feature bundle, while a marked tense or person change must produce the corresponding relational contrast. This constrains several singleton completions jointly through a finite opposition inventory, without assigning English words or changing known productions.

explicit_rivals.name: lexical-cell copying
explicit_rivals.consequence: Requires exact source-cell equality or one shared written key across the trilingual tables; this is the already closed GDT900 conjunction and is not reopened.

explicit_rivals.name: row-position-only tags
explicit_rivals.consequence: Treats each row position as an arbitrary local label, allowing a form to change person/tense content between complete readings; it predicts no preserved feature bundle or marked contrast.

design.source_owned_distinction: The content distinction survives global renaming: Latin, Persian and Cuman forms can all be renamed while the six-person and present/imperfect opposition remains. A row-order-only account loses this typed opposition; exact cell copying imposes a stronger lexical identity that the source does not require.
design.strongest_likely_failure: If the exposed complete target passages do not independently expose a finite person/number or tense contrast, feature bundles can be assigned arbitrarily and the proposal earns no discrimination. If the target is not multilingual or inflectional, the source analogy supplies no bridge.
design.falsifier: After freezing the complete target set and opposition inventory, no existential assignment preserves repeated-form bundles across readings, or the feature model makes exactly the same predictions as row-position-only tags for every held contrast. A failure cannot be repaired by changing productions, adding singleton meanings, or relabeling known values.
nearest_predecessors: IDEA000134 / GDT900: complete trilingual lexical-cell copying was exhaustively excluded; this proposal removes that equality premise and changes the tested consequence to typed feature opposition.
IDEA000317: existing Cumanicus person/time proposal targets a specific Y-AIIN-Y pattern; this card keeps the source feature inventory abstract and does not nominate that target form.
IDEA000122: shared-script multilingual architecture; this card does not posit a shared cipher key or paragraph language switch.
assumptions: Unknown target forms remain whole-space units; no EVA substring values are inferred.
All known target values and the 17 frozen productions remain fixed.
The complete target set, row boundaries and held opposition contrast must be frozen before any fit.
Codex Cumanicus is a source analogue for content relations only; it does not identify a target language or participant role.
design.selection_debt: No target field, writer, language, or source-to-target bridge is currently bound. This remains raw and unselected; a future review must name the complete target records and a held feature contrast before implementation.
